title: Amok

description.main: André Gelpke's Amok gathers twelve years of colour photographs, made between 2002 and 2014, into a personal commentary on the absurdities of ordinary life. Co-published by cpress and Spector Books in 2014 in a first edition of 800, with 194 colour photographs over 216 pages.
description.extended:
André Gelpke's Amok gathers twelve years of colour photographs, made between 2002 and 2014, into a personal commentary on the absurdities of ordinary life.

The book opens with Camus on the absurd and proceeds without captions or explanation. Gelpke works from his own motto, "Photography is a whore, never faithful, always feigning," and uses the camera to pick out small, unstaged situations from daily surroundings, ordering them the way a writer orders sentences. Published in November 2014 by cpress in Zurich and Spector Books in Leipzig, the first edition of 800 runs to 216 pages with 194 colour photographs, bound as a cloth-covered hardcover with the title printed as scattered white letterforms. Christof Nüssli edited the book with Gelpke and designed it; the texts are in English and German.

Gelpke (b. 1947) studied under Otto Steinert at the Folkwang School in Essen, co-founded the Visum agency in 1975 and left it three years later for his own projects. He is grouped with Michael Schmidt and Heinrich Riebesehl among the central author-photographers of post-war Germany, and from 1990 to 2012 he ran the photography programme at Zurich University of the Arts. The library also holds the 2015 reissue of his 1981 book Sex-Theater from the same publishers.
description.artist_bio: André Gelpke (b. 1947, Beienrode) studied under Otto Steinert at the Folkwang School in Essen, co-founded the Visum photo agency in 1975 and left it in 1978 for independent work. He headed photography studies at Zurich University of the Arts from 1990 to 2012. Solo exhibitions include the Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam, Museum Folkwang Essen and the Centre Pompidou.
